title: SS27 Boys' Harbour Club
summary: Nautical classics for boys: Breton stripes, navy and red, sailor-collar shirts for occasions and stripe sets for every day.
research_period: Pitti Bimbo 103, Florence, 24-25 June 2026; Playtime Paris, 28-30 June 2026; analysis July to November 2026
markets: Premium and mid-market childrenswear, Europe-led fairs, global retail

sections.heading: The story
sections.body: Sailor collars, navy blues and nautical details ran through Playtime Paris, with red and stripes as season-defining <sup>[1]</sup>. Cozmo showed striped tees and coordinated sets <sup>[2]</sup>; Loir Paris's sailor top was in MilK's selection <sup>[3]</sup>. Most SS27 kidswear sources describe collections across ages and genders. The evidence below is the fair record; the shapes, products and sizes are Forecut's application of it to boyswear, roughly ages 4 to 14.

sections.heading: Silhouettes
sections.body:
- Breton tee.
- Sailor-collar shirt for occasions.
- Bermuda shorts.
- Stripe set.

sections.heading: Fabrics
sections.body:
- Cotton jersey and interlock.
- Poplin and seersucker for shirts.
- Linen-cotton for shorts.

sections.heading: Trims and details
sections.body:
- Contrast tape on collars.
- Anchor-look buttons.
- Engineered stripes.

products: - Breton tees, sailor shirts, shorts, stripe sets, canvas shoes.
design_implications:
- Match stripes at side seams.
- Safety: no drawstrings or long cords at the hood, neck or waist, in line with EN 14682; test the attachment strength of buttons, snaps and decorations, and keep small detachable parts off baby and toddler pieces.
commercial_implications: - Stripes are reorder lines; sailor shirts are occasion buys.
